comment.narrative: ZLHR made submissions to various UN Special Rapporteurs highlighting its concerns on the PVO Bill. ZLHR participated in a virtual meeting with the UN Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Association and Assembly on 3 December 2021. On 17 December 2021 the Special Rapporteur on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and of association the Special Rapporteur on the promotion and protection of the right to freedom of opinion and expression the Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights defenders and the Special Rapporteur on the promotion and protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms while countering terrorism all drafted a joint public statement to the president highlighted their concerns with regard the PVO Bill noting that the Bill fails to comply with articles 19 and 22 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and FATF recommendation 8 the FATF requirements for a riskbased and consultative approach to the assessment of threats and vulnerabilities of terrorism abuse in the nonprofit sector and the requirement that legislative measures are necessary and proportionate in a democratic society. On 10 August 2022 ZLHR attended the Portfolio Committee on Justice Legal Parliamentary Affairs public hearings on the proposed Judicial Laws Amendment Bill. ZLHR participated and presented oral and written submissions on the impact of the Bill including its impact on the exercise of human rights. ZLHR submissions were based on a comprehensive legal analysis of the proposed Bill which seeks to provide for virtual court sittings in both civil and criminal proceedings and to align various provisions of judicial laws to the Constitution. While ZLHR welcomed the use of technology in Zimbabwes courts concerns were raised that the introduction of virtual sittings had the potential to hinder access to justice for many Zimbabweans. This would violate peoples right to a fair trial and right to nondiscrimination. On 22 September 2022 during the second reading of the Judicial Laws Amendment Bill in the National Assembly the Portfolio Committee on Justice Legal Parliamentary Affairs issued its report and almost all of ZLHRs submissions were adopted in that report.

title.narrative: % of finalised cases have favourable outcomes to ZLHR clients

description.narrative: Proportion of emergency and follow up legal cases that are taken up by ZLHR and get a positive outcome. ZLHR assistance includes provision of legal representation (oral or written) at police stations, other places of detention, in courts and other government institutions when necessary. Positive outcomes shall include the following results; released without charge, case dismissed, case discharged and acquitted.

comment.narrative: ZLHR reports every legal case taken up by the organisation through weekly reports. Updates to the cases are provided whenever lawyers attend to the case. Information of cases is also available as public information from the various courts.

title.narrative: % of surveyed HRDs by gender assisted who continue with their activities

description.narrative: A human rights defender is a person who individually or with others acts peacefully to promote and protect human rights enshrined in the constitution of Zimbabwe and other regional and international human rights instruments. ZLHR assistance includes provision of legal representation (oral or written) at police stations, other places of detention, in courts and other government institutions when necessary. Proportion of HRDs that continue with their work irrespective of persecution is an indicator of effectiveness of legal services in protecting human rights.
